name: Lichen Planus Pigmentosus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Lichen Planus Pigmentosus

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse or reticulated gray-brown to dark brown macules or patches predominantly on sun-exposed and flexural areas
Skin biopsy showing basal cell degeneration, pigment incontinence, and a lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrate
Lack of typical violaceous papules or plaques seen in classic lichen planus
Chronic, slowly progressive hyperpigmentation without significant pruritus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical pigmentation and confirmatory histopathology findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; exclusion of other pigmentary disorders is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse gray-brown to dark brown macular hyperpigmentation
Predominant involvement of sun-exposed and flexural areas
searchTerms: involvement of sun and fold areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of pruritic violaceous papules typical of classic lichen planus
searchTerms: no itchy purple bumps like lichen planus
absence of classic lichen planus rash

common.symptomName: Involvement of the face, neck, and upper trunk
searchTerms: skin involvement on face and neck
rash on upper chest and face
affected face, neck, and trunk skin

common.symptomName: Slowly progressive pigmentation over months to years
searchTerms: gradual darkening of skin over time
no rash on hands and feet
skin changes sparing palms and soles
slight skin flaking in rash areas
light scaling where rash is present

rare.symptomName: Nail changes such as longitudinal ridging or thinning
Associated lichen planus lesions elsewhere on the body
searchTerms: lichen planus lesions on other body parts

genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology showing basal cell vacuolar degeneration, pigment incontinence, and lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: History of preceding inflammatory skin condition
Lack of lichenoid infiltrate on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive pigmentation with ulceration or erosion
Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
Development of atypical or nodular skin lesions
references: Rao R, et al. Lichen Planus Pigmentosus: A Review. Indian J Dermatol Venereol Leprol. 2019.
Kumar J, et al. Clinical and Histopathological Features of Lichen Planus Pigmentosus. J Cutan Pathol. 2018.
